algorithm: Within each group: n=len(group); M=ceil(0.2*n); ns=floor(0.7*M); cap=M-ns; order=lexsort(pair ascending, score descending); screen=order[:ns]; hits=screen[hit1>0]; observed confirmed=sum(hit2[hits[:cap]]); oracle confirmed=min(cap,sum(hit2[hits])); verification order matters only if len(hits)>cap. No outcomes or models rerun.
implication: Under this static-prior screening set and P2 cap, a better verification order can add at most one observed confirmation over all 28 campaigns. Most additional value must change first-round screening, or use a separately costed policy/experiment.
limits: Oracle uses known R2 answers and is not deployable.
This bound fixes the first-round screen set; changing screening information or legal scheduling changes the problem.
14 exposed target cell lines; role assignments are not independent units.
This does not show that all agent, model, state or scheduling innovation has no value.
Unit-cost measurement replay; native plates, time and acquisition cost are not authenticated deployment savings.
